items.what: ONE profile carries tenant_id NULL with a non-platform role. ⚠⚠ THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES, and acting on it would have broken a working path. It said "ON DELETE SET NULL means every workspace deletion manufactures another" and recommended deactivating the profile. Measured 2026-08-20: (1) tenant_deletion_receipts holds ZERO rows — delete_tenant has NEVER been run, so no deletion has ever stranded anything; (2) delete_tenant already handles this anyway — it captures members BEFORE the cascade, deletes their profiles at step 6b, verifies none remain and reports profiles_removed, and its own comment records that an earlier version got that ordering wrong. THE REAL GENERATOR IS AN ABANDONED SIGNUP: the on_auth_user_created trigger runs handle_new_user(), which creates the profiles row with tenant_id NULL, and complete_signup assigns the tenant only later. Abandon between the two and the row persists. The live row is exactly that — spjamesvelez+1@gmail.com, a +1 alias of the founder’s own account, signed up 2026-07-09, last seen 2026-07-16, complete_signup never ran. ⚠ DO NOT "FIX" THE FOREIGN KEY. Switching profiles.tenant_id to ON DELETE CASCADE would move profile deletion to cascade time, where TEN of the thirteen FKs into profiles are NO ACTION and would block it — turning every future tenant deletion into an FK violation. The FK is a correct fallback, not the defect. A CHECK requiring a tenant for non-platform roles is equally wrong: handle_new_user creates the row before any tenant exists, so it would break signup itself. What is actually left is an accumulation risk, not a live one: a stranded row grants nothing (auth_tenant_id() returns NULL, so every membership check refuses), and closing this means either sweeping abandoned signups on a schedule or accepting them.

items.what: F-4 — dev lags production, so golden-path (certify’s only end-to-end write-path proof, and a CI job on every push) proves whatever schema dev happens to have. REOPENED 2026-08-20: closing this by rebuilding dev once was always going to decay, and the reason it cannot be fixed by replay is now measured. Of the 4 migrations dev was missing, THREE could not be applied to an empty environment because their assertions read production DATA rather than schema: 778 ("found no tenant with two distinctly named non-assistant employees", "the live-corpus replay saw ZERO pending escalations"), 789 ("no goal-having employee without an open plan"), and 790 ("no row carries disposition=cancelled") — the last of which is mine. Only 794, whose assertions read pg_proc, replayed. This is bigger than dev: a migration that asserts on production rows cannot be replayed into a restored backup or a new environment either, so it also undermines the restore drill. The migrations cannot simply be edited — they are applied, and the ledger keys on filename + checksum, so changing the files would break migration-files-match-ledger-checksums. The route forward is therefore to rebuild dev from the BASELINE (a schema dump, which does not replay assertions) on a schedule, not to replay migrations, and to stop new migrations asserting on operational rows.

verification.note: Unchanged pin, but note its known weakness: it compares ledger COUNTS, and two ledgers can hold the same number of DIFFERENT rows — dev carrying one production never had while missing one it does — which would read level while dev was wrong. scripts/sync-dev-migrations.mjs compares the SETS and reports dev-only rows separately; this pin is the cheap approximation certify runs. ── 2026-08-20: two mechanisms now exist. ci.yml runs scripts/sync-dev-migrations.mjs --apply --best-effort before golden-path (incremental, gets most of the way, cannot close the gap because of the data-asserting migrations), and .github/workflows/dev-rebuild.yml rebuilds dev nightly from a freshly regenerated baseline (a schema dump replays no assertions, so it is the only route to true parity). This item stays OPEN until a nightly has actually run and the two ledgers are level — the machinery existing is not the same as the gap being closed.

Until then the suite leaves test tenants behind on the dev project.

verification.note: ⚠ CONTENT, NEVER TIMESTAMPS. The obvious check compares deployed updated_at against file mtime; it was tried during the audit that found D-12 and flagged 61 of 65 functions, nearly all byte-identical to main — a ~94% false-positive rate is noise that trains people to ignore the section. This downloads each deployed ESZIP bundle, reads the module sources the runtime actually executes, and compares them to `git show origin/main:` through one normalizer (tsc transpile, comments dropped, redundant parens unwrapped at the AST level, whitespace and trailing commas normalized) because the bundle stores deno's EMIT, not the .ts. A bundle that will not parse is UNVERIFIABLE and throws, so it lands as F3 rather than as in-sync. EXCLUSIONS, each a hole that has to justify itself: de-answer (unmerged fix in flight in a parallel session — remove the exclusion when that branch lands) and mcp-demo-server (in the repo, never deployed; absent from the deployed list entirely). Denominators at first measurement: 64 deployed, 63 compared, 36 in sync, 27 drifted, 0 unverifiable, 1 in repo never deployed.
